hints: Calculate the forward driving force exerted by the cyclist using $P = F_D v$ with $P = 150\text{ W}$ and $v = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Apply Newton's second law along the horizontal road: $F_D - R = ma$, with resistance $R = 20\text{ N}$ and acceleration $a = 0.25\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Solve the resulting linear equation for the total mass $m$.
walkthrough:
State the relationship between power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D v$$
Substitute the known values $P = 150\text{ W}$ and $v = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the driving force:
$$150 = F_D (4)$$
Divide both sides by $4$:
$$F_D = \frac{150}{4} = 37.5\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law for the horizontal motion of the cyclist and bicycle:
$$\sum F = ma$$
$$F_D - R = ma$$
Substitute $F_D = 37.5\text{ N}$, resistance $R = 20\text{ N}$, and acceleration $a = 0.25\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$37.5 - 20 = m(0.25)$$
Subtract the numbers on the left-hand side:
$$17.5 = 0.25m$$
Divide both sides by $0.25$:
$$m = \frac{17.5}{0.25} = 70\text{ kg}$$
Thus the total mass of the cyclist and her bicycle is $70\text{ kg}$.

hints: Calculate the new driving force at constant speed $v = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{150}{3}$.
Because the cyclist ascends the hill at constant speed, acceleration is zero, so driving force equals resistance plus the component of weight down the slope: $F_D - R - mg\sin\theta = 0$.
Substitute $m = 70\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $R = 20\text{ N}$, solve for $\sin\theta$, and find $\theta$ in degrees.
walkthrough:
Determine the new driving force exerted by the cyclist on the hill:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{150\text{ W}}{3\text{ m s}^{-1}} = 50\text{ N}$$

Identify the forces acting parallel to the hill inclined at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal:
- Driving force up the hill: $F_D = 50\text{ N}$
- Resistance opposing motion down the hill: $R = 20\text{ N}$
- Component of total weight acting down the hill: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta$

State Newton's second law for motion at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$\sum F = ma = 0$$
$$F_D - R - mg\sin\theta = 0$$
Substitute $F_D = 50\text{ N}$, $R = 20\text{ N}$, $m = 70\text{ kg}$ (from part (a)), and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$50 - 20 - (70)(10)\sin\theta = 0$$
$$30 - 700\sin\theta = 0$$
$$700\sin\theta = 30$$
Divide both sides by $700$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{30}{700} = \frac{3}{70} \approx 0.042857$$

Take the inverse sine to find $\theta$:
$$\theta = \arcsin(0.042857) \approx 2.4567^\circ$$
Rounding to one decimal place as requested:
$$\theta = 2.5^\circ$$
Thus the angle of inclination of the hill is $2.5^\circ$.
